author: claude
title: The Rhythm of Rose Engine Guilloché

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: When people see a guilloché dial for the first time, they often think it's printed. But it's actually cut into the metal, isn't it?

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: That's right. Guilloché is a pattern of fine lines engraved into a surface. In English, it's also called engine-turning, because it's made with a special machine called an engine.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: And the most famous one is the rose engine?

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: Yes. A rose engine is a kind of lathe. The dial turns slowly while a sharp cutting tool touches the surface. At the same time, the dial moves slightly in and out, following a set of metal cams. That movement creates waves, petals and other repeating shapes.

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: Not at all. On a traditional machine, the craftsperson turns a handle and controls the pressure by feel. Each line is cut separately, and then the dial is moved a tiny bit for the next line.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: So one mistake can ruin the whole dial.

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: Exactly. If you cut too deep or lose your rhythm, you see it immediately. That's why many people describe the work as almost like music. You need a steady, calm rhythm.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: Why go to all that trouble?

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: Because of the light. The cut lines catch light at different angles, so the dial seems to move as you turn your wrist. Printing can't really copy that depth.
